title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 83 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 475–478 (Night 83, continuing directly from nights-82), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 83 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The fifth slave-girl gives the story of Moses and Shuʿayb at Midian and the dower of his labour, then sayings of the pious about neighbours and trust in God; the old woman follows with the devotions of the imams, above all al-Shāfiʿī, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the third and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-third night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.n: The print has بلعني, a misprint for بلغني, corrected here. It also runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ لِوَالِدِكَ فَدَخَلَ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَلَى شُعَيْبٍ وَالْعَشَاءُ مُهَيٌّ
sentences.tr: wa-qālati al-jāriyatu al-khāmisatu li-wālidika fa-dakhala mūsā ʿalayhi al-salāmu ʿalā shuʿaybin wa-al-ʿashāʾu muhayyun
sentences.l: And the fifth slave-girl said to your father: And Moses, peace be upon him, entered upon Shuʿayb, and the supper was prepared.
sentences.i: The fifth slave-girl said to your father: Moses, peace be upon him, went in to Shuʿayb when supper was ready.
sentences.n: The print spells the participle مهي, with a tanwin and no hamza; it is read as “made ready”, as in the previous night.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شُعَيْبٌ لِمُوسَى يَامُوسَى إِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ أُعْطِيَكَ أُجْرَةَ مَاسَقَيْتَ لَهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla shuʿaybun li-mūsā yā mūsā innī urīdu an uʿṭiyaka ujrata mā saqayta lahumā
sentences.l: And Shuʿayb said to Moses: O Moses, indeed I want that I give you the wage of what you watered for the two of them.
sentences.i: Shuʿayb said to Moses, “Moses, I wish to pay you for the watering you did for the two girls.”
sentences.n: The print joins اريد and أن into one word (اريدان), and يا to موسى; they are read as separate words.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ مُوسَى أَنَا مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ لَا نَبِيعُ شَيْأً مِنْ عَمَلِ الْآخِرَةِ بِمَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَفِضَّةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla mūsā anā min ahli baytin lā nabīʿu shayʾan min ʿamali al-ākhirati bi-mā ʿalā al-arḍi min dhahabin wa-fiḍḍatin
sentences.l: And Moses said: I am of the people of a house; we do not sell anything of the work of the hereafter for what is upon the earth of gold and silver.
sentences.i: Moses said, “I come from a family that does not sell any part of the work of the next life for all the gold and silver on earth.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شُعَيْبٌ يَا شَابُّ وَلَكِنْ أَنْتَ ضَيْفِى وَإِكْرَامُ الضَّيْفِ عَادَتِي وَعَادَةُ آبَائِي بِإِطْعَامِ الطَّعَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla shuʿaybun yā shābbu wa-lākin anta ḍayfī wa-ikrāmu al-ḍayfi ʿādatī wa-ʿādatu ābāʾī bi-iṭʿāmi al-ṭaʿāmi
sentences.l: And Shuʿayb said: O youth, but you are my guest, and the honouring of the guest is my custom and the custom of my fathers, by the feeding of food.
sentences.i: Shuʿayb said, “Young man, you are my guest, and honouring a guest by feeding him is my custom, as it was my fathers’.”

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَ مُوسَى فَأَكَلَ
sentences.tr: fa-jalasa mūsā fa-akala
sentences.l: And Moses sat, and ate.
sentences.i: So Moses sat down and ate.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شُعَيْبًا اسْتَأْجَرَ مُوسَى ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ أَيْ سِنِينَ وَجَعَلَ أُجْرَتَهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ تَزْوِيجَةُ إِحْدَى بِنْتَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna shuʿayban ista'jara mūsā thamāniya ḥijajin ayy sinīna wa-jaʿala ujratahu ʿalā dhālika tazwījahu iḥdā bintayhi
sentences.l: Then Shuʿayb hired Moses for eight pilgrimages — that is, years — and made his wage for that the marrying-off of one of his two daughters.
sentences.i: Then Shuʿayb hired Moses for eight years’ service, and made his wage for it marriage to one of his two daughters.
sentences.n: حجج is the plural of حَجَّة, literally “pilgrimage”; the text itself glosses it أي سنين, “that is, years”, and the verse quoted next uses it the same way. The print spells تزويجة with ة for ه (tazwījahu, “his marrying-off”), a habit of this edition.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عَمَلُ مُوسَى لِشُعَيْبٍ صَدَاقًا لَهَا كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى حِكَايَةً عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿamalu mūsā li-shuʿaybin ṣadāqan lahā kamā qāla taʿālā ḥikāyatan ʿanhu
sentences.l: And Moses’ work for Shuʿayb was a dower for her, as He, the Exalted, said, relating about him:
sentences.i: Moses’ labour for Shuʿayb was her dower, as God Most High says, relating Shuʿayb’s words:

sentences.t: اِنّي أُرِيْدُانْ أُنْكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ابْنَتَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ عَلَى انْ تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِنْدِكَ وَمَا أُرِيْدُانْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: innī urīdu an unkiḥaka iḥdā ibnatayya hātayni ʿalā an ta'jurunī thamāniya ḥijajin fa-in atmamta ʿashran fa-min ʿindika wa-mā urīdu an ashuqqa ʿalayka
sentences.l: Indeed I want that I marry you to one of my two daughters, these two, on condition that you hire yourself to me eight pilgrimages; and if you complete ten, then it is from you; and I do not want that I burden you.
sentences.i: “I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me eight years; and if you complete ten, that is of your own accord; and I do not wish to burden you.”
sentences.n: Qurʾān 28:27. The print points this verse, and its marks are kept as printed; it also runs أريد and أن together (أُرِيْدُانْ), as above.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لِبَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ وَكَانَ لَهُ مُدَّةٌ لَمْ يَرَهُ إِنَّكَ أَوْحَشْتَنِي لِأَنَّنِي مَا رَأَيْتُكَ مِنْ مُنْذُزَمَانٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla rajulun li-baʿḍi aṣḥābihi wa-kāna lahu muddatun lam yarahu innaka awḥashtanī li-annanī mā ra'aytuka min mundhu zamānin
sentences.l: And a man said to one of his companions — and there had been for him a while he had not seen him: Indeed you have made me lonely, because I have not seen you from since a time.
sentences.i: A man said to a friend he had not seen for some time, “I have missed you; it has been ages since I saw you.”
sentences.n: من منذ, “from since”, stacks two prepositions; the print also runs منذ and زمان together, and they are read as two words.

sentences.t: قَالَ اشْتَغَلْتُ عَنْكَ بِابْنِ شِهَابٍ أَتَعْرِفُهُ
sentences.tr: qāla ishtaghaltu ʿanka bi-ibni shihābin a-taʿrifuhu
sentences.l: He said: I was busy, away from you, with Ibn Shihāb; do you know him?
sentences.i: He said, “I have been taken up with Ibn Shihāb. Do you know him?”

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ هُوَجَارِي مِنْ مُنْذُ ثَلٰثِينَ سَنَةً إِلَّاأَنَّنِي لَمْ أُكَلِّمْهُ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam huwa jārī min mundhu thalāthīna sanatan illā annanī lam ukallimhu
sentences.l: He said: Yes, he is my neighbour from since thirty years — except that I have not spoken to him.
sentences.i: “Yes,” said the first, “he has been my neighbour for thirty years, though I have never spoken to him.”
sentences.n: The print runs several words together here (هوجاري, الانني); they are read as separate words. ثلثين is the print’s spelling of ثلاثين, without the alif. The print has الانني, with one alif dropped, for إلا أنني (“except that I”); it is corrected here, and the words stay run together as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ إِنَّكَ نَسِيتَ اللَّهَ فَنَسِيتَ جَارَكَ وَلَوْأَحْبَبْتَ اللَّهَ لَأَحْبَبْتَ جَارَكَ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ لِلْجَارِ عَلَى الْجَارِ حَقٌّ كَحَقِّ الْقَرَابَةِ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu innaka nasīta allāha fa-nasīta jāraka wa-law aḥbabta allāha la-aḥbabta jāraka a-mā ʿalimta anna li-al-jāri ʿalā al-jāri ḥaqqun ka-ḥaqqi al-qarābati
sentences.l: He said to him: Indeed you forgot God, so you forgot your neighbour; and if you had loved God, you would have loved your neighbour. Did you not know that for the neighbour upon the neighbour is a right, like the right of kinship?
sentences.i: The other said, “You have forgotten God, and so you have forgotten your neighbour. Had you loved God, you would have loved your neighbour. Do you not know that a neighbour has a claim upon his neighbour, like the claim of kinship?”
sentences.n: The print has حق without the alif of the accusative (حقًّا, which Classical grammar wants after أنّ with its predicate placed first); it is read as printed, as a nominative.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ حُذَيْفَةُ دَخَلْنَا مَكَّةَ مَعَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَدْهَمَ وَكَانَ شَقِيقٌ الْبَلْخِيُّ قَدْحَجَّ فِي تِلْكَ السَّنَةِ فَاجْتَمَعْنَا فِى الطَّوَافِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ḥudhayfatu dakhalnā makkata maʿa ibrāhīma ibni adhama wa-kāna shaqīqun al-balkhiyyu qad ḥajja fī tilka al-sanati fa-ajtamaʿnā fī al-ṭawāfi
sentences.l: And Ḥudhayfa said: We entered Mecca with Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, and Shaqīq al-Balkhī had made the pilgrimage in that year; so we gathered at the circumambulation.
sentences.i: Ḥudhayfa said, “We entered Mecca with Ibrāhīm ibn Adham. Shaqīq of Balkh had also made the pilgrimage that year, and we all met during the circling of the Kaʿba.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِشَقِيقٍ مَاشَأْنُكُمْ فِى بِلَادِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ibrāhīmu li-shaqīqin mā shaʾnukum fī bilādikum
sentences.l: And Ibrāhīm said to Shaqīq: What is your affair in your lands?
sentences.i: Ibrāhīm said to Shaqīq, “What is your way of life in your country?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَقِيقٌ إِنَّنَا إِذَا رُزِقْنَا أَكَلْنَا وَإِذَاجُعْنَا صَبَرْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla shaqīqun innanā idhā ruziqnā akalnā wa-idhā jʿnā ṣabarnā
sentences.l: And Shaqīq said: Indeed we, when we are provided, we eat, and when we are hungry, we are patient.
sentences.i: Shaqīq said, “When we are given provision, we eat; when we go hungry, we are patient.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ كَذَا تَفْعَلُ كِلَابُ بَلْخٍ وَلَكِنَّنَا إِذَا رُزِقْنَا آثَرْنَا وَإِذَا جُعْنَا شَكَرْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla kadhā tafʿalu kilābu balkhin wa-lākinnanā idhā ruziqnā ātharnā wa-idhā jʿnā shakarnā
sentences.l: And he said: Thus the dogs of Balkh do! But we, when we are provided, we prefer others, and when we are hungry, we give thanks.
sentences.i: He said, “That is what the dogs of Balkh do! When we are given provision, we put others first; when we go hungry, we give thanks.”

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَ شَقِيقٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ أُسْتَاذِي
sentences.tr: fa-jalasa shaqīqun bayna yaday ibrāhīma wa-qāla lahu anta ustādhī
sentences.l: And Shaqīq sat between the hands of Ibrāhīm and said to him: You are my master.
sentences.i: Shaqīq sat down before Ibrāhīm and said, “You are my teacher.”

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِمْرَانَ سَأَلَ رَجُلٌ حَاتِمًا الْأَصَمَّ فَقَالَ مَا أَمْرُكَ فِى التَّوَكُّلِ عَلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: wa-qāla muḥammadu bnu ʿimrāna saʾala rajulun ḥātiman al-aṣamma fa-qāla mā amruka fī al-tawakkuli ʿalā allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān said: A man asked Ḥātim the Deaf, and said: What is your matter in trust upon God the Exalted?
sentences.i: Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān said: A man asked Ḥātim al-Aṣamm, “What is your way in relying on God Most High?”

sentences.t: قَالَ عَلَى خَصْلَتَيْنِ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ رِزْقِي لَايَأْكُلُهُ غَيْرِي فَاطْمَأَنَّتْ نَفْسِي بِهِ وَعَلِمْتُ أَنِّي لَمْ أُخْلَقْ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ فَاسْتَحَيْتُ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: qāla ʿalā khaṣlatayni ʿalimtu anna rizqī lā yaʾkuluhu ghayrī fa-iṭmaʾannat nafsī bihi wa-ʿalimtu annī lam ukhlaq min ghayri ʿilmi allāhi fa-istaḥaytu minhu
sentences.l: He said: On two qualities: I knew that my provision no one other than I will eat, so my soul was at rest in it; and I knew that I was not created without God’s knowledge, so I was ashamed before Him.
sentences.i: He said, “On two things: I knew that no one but I will eat my provision, so my soul was at ease about it; and I knew that I was not created without God’s knowledge, so I felt shame before Him.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَأَخَّرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَتَقَدَّمَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ وَالِدِكَ تِسْعَ مَرَّاتٍ
sentences.tr: thumma ta'akhkharati al-jāriyatu al-khāmisatu wa-taqaddamati al-ʿajūzu wa-qabbalati al-arḍa bayna wālidika tisʿa marrātin
sentences.l: Then the fifth slave-girl drew back, and the old woman came forward and kissed the ground between your father, nine times.
sentences.i: Then the fifth slave-girl drew back, and the old woman came forward and kissed the ground nine times before your father.
sentences.n: The print has بين والدك, “between your father”, without يدي, “the hands of”; the usual phrase is بين يدي والدك, “before your father”, and it is translated so. The text is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ قَدْسَمِعْتُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ مَا تَكَلَّمَ بِهِ الْجَمِيعُ فِي بَابِ الزُّهْدِ وَأَنَا تَابِعَةٌ لَهُنَّ فَأَذْكُرُ بَعْضَ مَا بَلَغَنِي عَنْ أَكَابِرِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat qad samiʿtu ayyuhā al-maliku mā takallama bihi al-jamīʿu fī bābi al-zuhdi wa-anā tābiʿatun lahunna fa-adhkuru baʿḍa mā balaghanī ʿan akābiri al-mutaqaddimīna
sentences.l: And she said: I have heard, O king, what all of them spoke in the chapter of renunciation, and I am a follower of them; so I will mention some of what has reached me from the greatest of the foregoers.
sentences.i: She said, “O king, I have heard what all of them have said on the subject of renunciation, and I follow them; so let me tell some of what has reached me about the great men of old.”

sentences.t: قِيلَ كَانَ الْإِمَامُ الشَّافِعِيُّ يُقَسِّمُ اللَّيْلَ ثَلٰثَةَ أَقْسَامٍ الثُّلُثُ الْأَوَّلُ لِلْعِلْمِ وَالثَّانِي لِلنَّوْمِ وَالثَّالِثُ لِلتَّهَجُّدِ
sentences.tr: qīla kāna al-imāmu al-shāfiʿiyyu yuqassimu al-layla thalāthata aqsāmin al-thulthu al-awwalu li-al-ʿilmi wa-al-thānī li-al-nawmi wa-al-thālithu li-al-tahajjudi
sentences.l: It was said: The imam al-Shāfiʿī used to divide the night three parts: the first third for knowledge, and the second for sleep, and the third for night-vigil.
sentences.i: It is said that Imam al-Shāfiʿī divided the night into three parts: the first third for learning, the second for sleep, and the third for night prayer.
sentences.n: ثلثة is the print’s spelling of ثلاثة, without the alif. Al-Shāfiʿī (d. 820) is the founder of one of the four Sunni schools of law, and Abū Ḥanīfa (d. 767), named next, of another.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْإِمَامُ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ يُحْيِي نِصْفَ اللَّيْلِ فَأَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ إِنْسَانٌ وَهُوَ يَمْشِي وَقَالَ لِآخَرَإنَّ هَذَا يُحْيِي اللَّيْلَ كُلَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-imāmu abū ḥanīfata yuḥyī niṣfa al-layli fa-ashāra ilayhi insānun wa-huwa yamshī wa-qāla li-ākhara anna hādhā yuḥyī al-layla kullahu
sentences.l: And the imam Abū Ḥanīfa used to bring-to-life half the night; and a person pointed at him as he was walking, and said to another: Indeed this one brings-to-life the night, all of it.
sentences.i: Imam Abū Ḥanīfa used to spend half the night in worship. Someone pointed him out as he walked by and said to another, “That man keeps the whole night awake in prayer.”
sentences.n: The print has الميل, a misprint for الليل, corrected here. It also runs لآخر and أن together (لآخران). يحيي الليل, “brings the night to life”, is the idiom for spending it in wakeful worship.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ إِنِّي أَسْتَحِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَنْ أُوصَفَ بِمَالَيْسَ فِيَّ فَصَارَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ يُحْيِي اللَّيْلَ كُلَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa dhālika qāla innī astaḥī mina allāhi an ūṣafa bi-mā laysa fiyya fa-ṣāra baʿda dhālika yuḥyī al-layla kullahu
sentences.l: And when he heard that, he said: Indeed I am ashamed before God that I be described by what is not in me. And after that he came to bring the night to life, all of it.
sentences.i: When he heard this he said, “I am ashamed before God to be described as what I am not,” and from then on he spent the whole night in prayer.
sentences.n: The print runs بما and ليس together (بماليس); they are read as two words.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الرَّبِيعُ كَانَ الشَّافِعِيُّ يَخْتِمُ الْقُرْآنَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً كُلَّ ذَلِكَ فِى الصَّلٰوةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-rabīʿu kāna al-shāfiʿiyyu yakhtimu al-qurʾāna fī shahri ramaḍāna sabʿīna marratan kulla dhālika fī al-ṣalāti
sentences.l: And al-Rabīʿ said: al-Shāfiʿī used to complete the Qurʾān in the month of Ramadan seventy times, all of that in the prayer.
sentences.i: Al-Rabīʿ said, “Al-Shāfiʿī used to recite the whole Qurʾān seventy times in the month of Ramadan, all of it in his prayers.”
sentences.n: الصلوة is the older spelling of الصلاة, with a written wāw for the long ā; it is pointed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الشَّافِعِىُّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مَاشَبِعْتُ مِنْ خُبْزِ الشَّعِيرِ عَشْرَسِنِينَ لِأَنَّ الشِّبَعَ يُقَسِّى الْقَلْبَ وَيُزِيلُ الْفِطْنَةَ وَيَجْلِبُ النَّوْمَ وَيُضْعِفُ صَاحِبَهُ عَنِ الْقِيَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-shāfiʿiyyu raḍiya allāhu ʿanhu mā shabiʿtu min khubzi al-shaʿīri ʿashra sinīna li-anna al-shibaʿa yuqassī al-qalba wa-yuzīlu al-fiṭnata wa-yajlibu al-nawma wa-yuḍʿifu ṣāḥibahu ʿani al-qiyāmi
sentences.l: And al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said: I have not been sated with barley bread for ten years, because satiety hardens the heart and removes shrewdness and brings sleep and weakens its possessor from standing.
sentences.i: Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said, “For ten years I have not eaten my fill of barley bread, because a full stomach hardens the heart, dulls the wits, brings on sleep, and leaves a man too weak to stand in prayer.”
sentences.n: The print runs ما and شبعت, and عشر and سنين, together; they are read as separate words. The last word, القيام, “standing”, is the standing of the night prayer.

sentences.t: وَرُوِيَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ السُّكَّرِيِّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ كُنْتُ أَنَا وَعُمَرُ نَتَحَدَّثُ فَقَالَ لِي مَا رَأَيْتُ أَوْرَعَ وَلَا أَفْصَحَ مِنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ الشَّافِعِيِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ruwiya ʿan ʿabdi allāhi bni muḥammadin al-sukkariyyi annahu qāla kuntu anā wa-ʿumaru nataḥaddathu fa-qāla lī mā ra'aytu awraʿa wa-lā afṣaḥa min muḥammadi bni idrīsa al-shāfiʿiyyi
sentences.l: And it was related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Sukkarī that he said: I and ʿUmar were conversing, and he said to me: I have not seen one more scrupulous, nor more eloquent, than Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī.
sentences.i: It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Sukkarī that he said, “ʿUmar and I were talking together, and he said to me, ‘I have never seen anyone more scrupulous or more eloquent than Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī.’”

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّنِي خَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَالْحَارِثُ بْنُ لَبِيبٍ الصَّفَّارُ وَكَانَ الْحَارِثُ تِلْمِيذَ الْمُزَنِيِّ وَكَانَ صَوْتُهُ حَسَنًا
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqa annanī kharajtu anā wa-al-ḥārithu bnu labībin al-ṣaffāru wa-kāna al-ḥārithu tilmīdha al-muzaniyyi wa-kāna ṣawtuhu ḥasanan
sentences.l: And it happened that I went out, I and al-Ḥārith ibn Labīb the brass-worker — and al-Ḥārith was a disciple of al-Muzanī, and his voice was good.
sentences.i: It happened that I went out with al-Ḥārith ibn Labīb the brass-worker, a pupil of al-Muzanī, who had a beautiful voice.

sentences.t: فَقَرَأَ قَوْلَهُ تَعَالَي هَذَا يَوْمٌ لَايَنْطِقُونَ وَلَا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-qaraʾa qawlahu taʿālā hādhā yawmun lā yanṭiqūna wa-lā yu'dhanu lahum fa-yaʿtadhirūna
sentences.l: And he recited His saying, the Exalted: This is a day on which they do not speak, nor is permission given them, so that they make excuse.
sentences.i: He recited the words of God Most High: “This is a day on which they cannot speak, nor are they permitted to offer excuses.”
sentences.n: The print has فقراً, with a stray tanwin, a misprint for فقرأ, “he recited”, corrected here. The verse is Qurʾān 77:35–36; the ending of تعالي is spelled with ي.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ الْإِمَامَ الشَّافِعِيَّ تَغَيَّرَ لَوْنُهُ وَاقْشَعَرَّ جِلْدُهُ وَاضْطَرَبَ اضْطِرَابًا شَدِيدًا وَخَرَّ مُغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ra'aytu al-imāma al-shāfiʿiyya taghayyara lawnuhu wa-aqshaʿarra jildahu wa-iḍṭaraba iḍṭirāban shadīdan wa-kharra mughshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And I saw the imam al-Shāfiʿī: his colour changed, and his skin bristled, and he trembled a violent trembling, and fell down swooned upon him.
sentences.i: Then I saw Imam al-Shāfiʿī: his colour changed, his skin shuddered, he shook violently and fell down in a faint.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ مَقَامِ الْكَذَّابِينَ وَإِعْرَاضِ الْغَافِلِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa qāla aʿūdhu bi-allāhi min maqāmi al-kadhdhābīna wa-iʿrāḍi al-ghāfilīna
sentences.l: And when he came to, he said: I seek refuge with God from the standing-place of the liars and the turning-away of the heedless.
sentences.i: When he came to, he said, “I seek refuge in God from the station of the liars and the aversion of the heedless.”

sentences.t: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ خَشَعَتّْ قُلُوبُ الْعَارِفِينَ اللَّهُمَّ هَبْلِي غُفْرَانَ ذُنُوبِي مِنْ جُودِكَ وَجَمِّلْنِي بِسَتْرِكَ وَاعْفُ عَنْ تَقْصِيرِي بِكَرَمِ وَجْهِكَ
sentences.tr: allāhumma laka khashaʿat qulūbu al-ʿārifīna allāhumma hab lī ghufrāna dhunūbī min jūdika wa-jammilnī bi-satrika wa-ʿfu ʿan taqṣīrī bi-karami wajhika
sentences.l: O God, to You the hearts of the knowers have been humbled. O God, give me forgiveness of my sins out of Your generosity, and beautify me with Your veil, and pardon my falling-short by the generosity of Your face.
sentences.i: O God, before You the hearts of the knowers are humbled. O God, grant me, out of Your bounty, forgiveness of my sins; adorn me with Your covering, and pardon my shortcomings for the sake of Your generous face.
sentences.n: The print puts a shadda on the tā’ of خشعتّ, which looks like a stray mark; it is kept, and the verb is read khashaʿat, “were humbled”. The print also runs هب and لي together (هبلي). العارفين, “the knowers”, are those who know God by direct experience, the mystics.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُمْتُ وَانْصَرَفْتُ
sentences.tr: thumma qumtu wa-inṣaraftu
sentences.l: Then I rose and went away.
sentences.i: Then I got up and left.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ بَعْضُ الثِّقَاةِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ بَغْدَادَ كَانَ الشَّافِعِيُّ بِهَا فَجَلَسْتُ عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ لِأَتَوَضَّأَ لِلصَّلٰوةِ إِذْمَرَّبِي إِنْسَانٌ فَقَالَ لِي يَاغُلَامُ أَحْسِنْ وُضُؤَكَ يُحْسِنِ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ فِى الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla baʿḍu al-thiqāti fa-lammā dakhaltu baghdāda kāna al-shāfiʿiyyu bihā fa-jalastu ʿalā al-shāṭiʾi li-atawaḍḍaʾa li-al-ṣalāti idh marra bī insānun fa-qāla lī yā ghulāmu aḥsin wuḍūʾaka yuḥsini allāhu ilayka fī al-dunyā wa-al-ākhirati
sentences.l: And one of the trustworthy said: When I entered Baghdad, al-Shāfiʿī was in it; and I sat on the bank to perform ablution for the prayer, when a person passed by me and said to me: O boy, make good your ablution; God will make good to you in the world and the hereafter.
sentences.i: One of the reliable narrators said: “When I came to Baghdad, al-Shāfiʿī was there. I sat on the riverbank to make my ablutions for prayer, when a man passed by and said to me, ‘Young man, perform your ablutions well, and God will be good to you in this world and the next.’”
sentences.n: The print runs several words together (لاتوضأ, اذمربي, ياغلام); they are read as separate words. وضؤك is the print’s spelling of وضوءك. الثقاة is read as a plural of ثقة, “trustworthy”, here meaning reliable transmitters.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتُّ وَإِذَا بِرَجُلٍ يَتْبَعُهُ جَمَاعَةٌ فَأَسْرَعْتُ فِي وُضُوئِي وَجَعَلْتُ أَقْفُو أَثَرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafattu wa-idhā bi-rajulin yatbaʿuhu jamāʿatun fa-asraʿtu fī wuḍūʾī wa-jaʿaltu aqfū atharahu
sentences.l: And I turned, and behold, with a man a group following him; so I hurried in my ablution and began to follow his track.
sentences.i: I turned and saw a man with a crowd following him, so I hurried through my ablutions and set out after him.
sentences.n: After وإذا of surprise the بِـ only marks what appears: “and behold, a man”.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ وَقَالَ هَلْ لَكَ مِنْ حَاجَةٍ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ تُعَلِّمُنِي مِمَّا عَلَّمَكَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata ilayya wa-qāla hal laka min ḥājatin fa-qultu naʿam tuʿallimunī mimmā ʿallamaka allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: And he turned to me and said: Have you any need? And I said: Yes — that you teach me of what God the Exalted has taught you.
sentences.i: He turned to me and asked, “Do you need anything?” I said, “Yes — that you teach me something of what God Most High has taught you.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَنْ صَدَقَ اللَّهَ نَجَا وَمَنْ أَشْفَقَ عَلَى دِينِهِ سَامَ مِنَ الرَّدَى وَمَنْ زَهِدَ فِى الدُّنْيَا قَرَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ غَدًا أَفَلَا أَزِيدُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iʿlam anna man ṣadaqa allāha najā wa-man ashfaqa ʿalā dīnihi sāma mina al-radā wa-man zahida fī al-dunyā qarrat ʿaynāhu ghadan a-fa-lā azīduka
sentences.l: And he said: Know that whoever is true to God is saved, and whoever takes care for his religion is safe from destruction, and whoever renounces in the world, his two eyes are cooled tomorrow. Shall I not add to you?
sentences.i: He said, “Know that whoever is true to God is saved; whoever cares for his faith is safe from ruin; and whoever renounces this world will have joy tomorrow. Shall I tell you more?”
sentences.n: The print has سام, which does not fit; the sense wants سَلِمَ, “is safe”, and it is translated so, but the letters are kept as printed and doubtful. قرّت عيناه, “his eyes cooled”, is the idiom for gladness.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ بَلَى قَالَ كُنْ فِى الدُّنْيَا زَاهِدًا وَفِى الْآخِرَةِ رَاغِبًا وَاصْدُقْ فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِكَ تَنْجُ مَعَ النَّاجِينَ
sentences.tr: qultu balā qāla kun fī al-dunyā zāhidan wa-fī al-ākhirati rāghiban wa-iṣduq fī jamīʿi umūrika tanju maʿa al-nājīna
sentences.l: I said: Yes. He said: Be in the world one who renounces, and in the hereafter one who desires; and be truthful in all your affairs; you will be saved with the saved.
sentences.i: I said, “Yes.” He said, “Be an ascetic in this world and an eager seeker in the next, and be truthful in all your affairs; you will be saved with the saved.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَضَى فَسَأَلْتُ عَنْهُ فَقِيلَ لِي هَذَا الْإِمَامُ الشَّافِعِيُّ
sentences.tr: thumma maḍā fa-saʾaltu ʿanhu fa-qīla lī hādhā al-imāmu al-shāfiʿiyyu
sentences.l: Then he went on, and I asked about him, and it was said to me: This is the imam al-Shāfiʿī.
sentences.i: Then he went on his way. I asked about him and was told, “That is Imam al-Shāfiʿī.”

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْإِمَامُ الشَّافِعِىُّ يَقُولُ وَدِدْتُ أَنَّ النَّاسَ يَنْتَفِعُونَ بِهَذَا الْعِلْمِ عَلَى أَنْ لَا يُنْسَبَ إِلَيَّ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-imāmu al-shāfiʿiyyu yaqūlu wadidtu anna al-nāsa yantafiʿūna bi-hādhā al-ʿilmi ʿalā an lā yunsaba ilayya minhu shayʾun
sentences.l: And the imam al-Shāfiʿī used to say: I would love that the people benefit by this knowledge, on condition that nothing of it be ascribed to me.
sentences.i: Imam al-Shāfiʿī used to say, “I would love for people to benefit from this knowledge, provided that none of it be ascribed to me.”

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, with its rhyme on -āḥ, as in every night.
